## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `75a0ac45f8b60d523b233fcbef0ecf53d6968932`
Local-runs: none
Scope: .github/workflows/release.yml, .github/workflows/lint.yml, docs/releases-maintenance.md, scripts/ci/scheduled-full-run.mjs, scripts/ci/snapshot-next.mjs, scripts/pm/fleet-write/validate.mjs, scripts/release-snapshot-publish.sh + docs/adr/0125-release-approval-gate-replaces-the-typed-version.md (Amendment 2026-11-05), scripts/release-pending-publish.mjs, scripts/release-publish.sh, scripts/release-verify-npm.mjs, scripts/release-dist-tags.mjs, scripts/release-spec-changes.sh, scripts/release-github-releases.mjs, .changeset/config.json, .github/actions/setup-workspace/action.yml, AGENTS.md (Prime Directive 15)

Independent read of PR #30799 at the head above, net diff `origin/main...claude/issue-30591-next-snapshot-lane` (7 files, +1716 −37), against ADR-0125's `## Amendment (2026-11-05, #29466)` "What the lane must satisfy", ruling 6663894403, card #30591 and its five comments, and the head's check-runs. The tree was judged, not the PR body. All line numbers are the head's.

**Check-runs on the head (the gate verdicts):** at the last poll (2026-11-06, after 03:48Z) every check-run had completed: 49 `success`, 14 `skipped`, 0 `failure`, none in progress. Among them: `Governed Surface Queue Guard` success; `PR-body guards (claim · duplicate · Part-of · single-writer path)` success; `Lint · CI, release & engine gates` success with its step `Snapshot lane guard self-test` (`snapshot-next.mjs --self-test`) `success` and `Release version-commit selection self-test` `success`; `Lint · PM dispatch-gates` success; `Lint · repo & tooling gates` success (carries `check:pm-fleet-write-validate`); `Check Changeset` success under `skip-changeset`.

### ① Derived judgments

Each amendment requirement, read in the tree, then the attempts to break it.

**The guard and the debut rule — met.**
- Debut: `scripts/ci/snapshot-next.mjs:168-178` `debutRefusals` refuses a fixed-group member whose abbreviated packument is 404 (`readRegistryState` :282-305 returns `null` on 404, throws `RegistryUnreadable` on anything else, so an unread member is never read as absent) and one with versions but no `latest`. `preflight` (:346-362) runs it over `.changeset/config.json`'s one fixed group (`fixedGroup` :140-146) and refuses too when the publishable set (non-private workspace packages, `listWorkspacePackages`) differs from the group (`groupProblems` :149-160) — load-bearing, because `changeset publish` v3's `getUnpublishedPackages` publishes every non-private package absent from the registry regardless of `ignore`, so a publishable non-member could otherwise debut at its own version. Live: `npm view @objectstack/service-push` answers E404 today, so the lane refuses until the stable lane debuts it — exactly the amendment's case.
- Where it binds: the preflight job `snapshot-next-preflight` (`release.yml:2182`) carries no `environment:` and runs `snapshot-next.mjs preflight` at :2261; `snapshot-next` needs it with `if: success() && …` (:2281-2284), so a refusal queues no deployment. The debut rule and the RC-cycle rule are re-read after the approval at :2358 (`preflight --record`).
- Tag: the publish is one line, `changeset publish --tag next --no-git-tag` (`scripts/release-snapshot-publish.sh:47`), called once from the job (:2412). In `@changesets/cli@3.0.3` (the lockfile's pin; read from the published tarball, `dist/getPublishPlan.mjs` `getReleaseTag(publishedState, preState, tag) { if (tag) return tag; … }`) the CLI tag overrides every release's tag. The overrides that beat the CLI are checked by `guard` (:390-453) before the publish (:2398, pinned to precede :2412 by `snapshotWiring` :664): `publishConfig.tag`, repo and package `.npmrc` `tag=` lines and `npm_config_tag`/`NPM_CONFIG_TAG` (`tagOverrideProblems` :196-212, value never printed), the `@changesets/cli` major (:394-397), one `0.0.0-next-\d{14}` version across the whole group (`versionProblems` :181-193), the publish plan equal to the group with no `tag-only` entry (`planProblems` :221-244), and every packed manifest's name, version, `publishConfig.tag`, no `workspace:` range, every intra-group range satisfied by the snapshot (`packedManifestProblems` :247-269). `verify` (:456-487, step :2427) then reads `next` back at the snapshot on every member and treats a `latest` that moved onto the snapshot as an incident (`::error::INCIDENT`, never a counter-publish).
- Break attempts: (a) another tag via the command — the self-test pins the script to exactly that line and refuses `--tag latest` and a line without `--no-git-tag` (:850-851); (b) via `publishConfig`/`.npmrc`/env — refused by `guard`; (c) via pre mode (changesets publishes under the pre tag) — refused by `preModeRefusal` before and after approval, and changesets itself refuses `--tag` and `--snapshot` in pre mode (`dist/index.mjs` "Releasing under custom tag is not allowed in pre mode", "Snapshot release is not allowed in pre mode"); (d) via a first publish — refused by the debut rule; a publishable package outside the group is refused by `groupProblems` and by `planProblems`. I found no path from this lane to a dist-tag other than `next`, nor a debut.

**Dispatch-only and exclusive — met, strictly subtractive.**
- The input `snapshot_next` (`release.yml:252-261`, boolean, default false). Both new jobs run only on `github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && inputs.snapshot_next && !inputs.refresh_version_pr` (:2184-2186, :2281-2284); on `push` and `schedule` the `inputs` context is empty and the predicate is false.
- The three stable guards gain `&& !inputs.snapshot_next` inside their dispatch branch only: `release-integrity` :997, `full-battery` :1562, `publish` :1657 — the same shape as `!inputs.refresh_version_pr`. `version-pr` (:299, `schedule || (dispatch && refresh_version_pr)`), `stale-prompts` (:1495) and `docker` (:2124, `!cancelled() && (outputs.published == 'true' …)` over two skipped `needs`, so false) are untouched.
- Break attempts: snapshot + `force` → `release-integrity` skipped by :997; `full-battery`/`publish` skipped both by their own `!inputs.snapshot_next` and by `success()` over the skipped need; `docker` skipped; the snapshot jobs never read `inputs.force` (pinned :639, :856). Snapshot + `refresh_version_pr` → `version-pr` alone, the snapshot jobs refuse on `!inputs.refresh_version_pr`. A stable dispatch (neither input) or a push → neither snapshot job. All of this is evaluated by fleet-write's own `jobsStartedBy` in the self-test's exclusivity battery (:859-884), with a firing control (:881-884: release-integrity without the negation does start on a snapshot dispatch); `validate.mjs:1460-1461` pins the eight-job roster and that the relay's refresh stroke skips both snapshot jobs. The relay refuses any input but `refresh_version_pr: true` by name (validate.mjs:1435-1437), so no seat can dispatch the lane through it (Prime Directive 15).
- `stale-prompts` runs on a snapshot dispatch (its `if:` is unchanged); it only cancels waiting push-lane runs whose version is on npm, so this is an extra sweep, not a stable-lane change.

**The commit, distance zero — met.**
- `scheduled-full-run.mjs:912-956` `releaseGateVerdict` gains `chosen` rows (run id, event, head, distance, conclusion) and `distanceZero`; with `requireDistanceZero` a deciding run on an ancestor refuses, naming its workflow (:951). `selectSnapshotCommit` (:981-990) walks first-parent history from the dispatched head and returns the first offset whose strict verdict passes, so selection and gate cannot disagree. `releaseGateRecord` (:962-972) is built from the verdict alone; `--json` puts one record on stdout and the prose on stderr (`emit` :1205-1208).
- The preflight (:2225-2250) refuses off `main`, selects with `--snapshot-commit --from "$GITHUB_SHA" --json`, re-asks `--release-gate --release-commit C --require-distance-zero --json` and checks `.ok && .distanceZero && .requireDistanceZero && .releaseCommit == C` with `jq -e`, then detaches to C so the RC-cycle, debut and dry-run reads happen on the selected tree. The publish job checks out that exact commit (`ref:` :2305, `fetch-depth: 0`), refuses an empty ref, a HEAD that is not it, a shallow clone, and a commit that is not an ancestor of `refs/remotes/origin/main` as just fetched (:2320-2340). Main moving between the two jobs changes nothing: the published tree is C, judged at distance zero; a force-push removing C fails the ancestry check.
- The stable gate is unchanged when the flag is absent: `requireDistanceZero` defaults false; the recorded fixture still passes 0524c1619b at distance 3 (self-test :2636-2650).

**Not during an RC cycle — met in the mechanism it must defeat; one should-fix on the tree it reads (below).** `preModeRefusal` (:122-137) refuses `mode: pre`, an unknown mode and unparseable JSON; `exit` and absence pass. Run in the preflight job before any deployment and again after approval. `.changeset/pre.json` is absent on `origin/main` today.

**Workspace only — met.** The bare `pnpm exec changeset version --snapshot next` (:2367; `pnpm run version` is forbidden in the lane by :602 and pinned by :857), followed by an assertion that `@objectstack/cli` is `0.0.0-next-` + 14 digits. The job holds `contents: read` (:2300) and a checkout with `persist-credentials: false` (:2307), so nothing in it can push; `.changeset/config.json` has `"commit": false`; `--no-git-tag` creates no tag. `FORBIDDEN_IN_SNAPSHOT` (:597-606) pins both jobs and the script against `git push`, `gh release`, `npm dist-tag`, a direct `npm|pnpm|yarn publish`, the stable post-publish scripts, `--prepare`/`--attach` and `docker-publish.yml`. The consumed changesets and rendered CHANGELOGs stay in the runner. I found no path by which a consumed changeset, a CHANGELOG, a tag or a version bump reaches git.

**The approval screen — met.** `name: Snapshot next of main ${{ needs.snapshot-next-preflight.outputs.commit-short }} (awaiting approval)` (:2276) at `environment: release` (:2280): says `next` snapshot, names the main commit. `PUBLISH_JOB_NAME` is `/^Publish (\S+) to npm \(awaiting approval\)$/` (`release-pending-publish.mjs:282`); the rendered name does not match, pinned at :628 and :844-845. In the sweep, a waiting snapshot run has no job matching `PUBLISH_JOB_NAME` and falls into `untouched` ("no publish job waiting at an environment", :1008-1010); `in-flight` compares an exact `Publish ${version} to npm (awaiting approval)` string. Neither `release-pending-publish` nor `stale-prompts` can read the snapshot prompt as a stable one, and the sweep never cancels a dispatch run.

**Concurrency — right.** `release-snapshot-next-${{ github.ref }}`, `cancel-in-progress: false` (:2294-2296), pinned never to be `release-publish-*` (:643, :848). This is what the amendment's D5 reading requires: a snapshot waiting at the environment holds its own group, so it neither hides nor evicts a stable prompt (the 17.4.0 shape) and is not evicted by one. The residual, accepted by that design: a maintainer approving a stable publish and a snapshot in the same minutes can leave `next` mixed across members (the stable's `release-dist-tags.mjs --apply` and the snapshot's `--tag next` racing), which `verify` surfaces as red `pending`, never as a `latest` move. Not a finding.

**The dry run — met.** `dryRun` (:513-568) runs the registry preflight (reported), refuses a dirty tree, runs the bare version step, then `guard` with a pack (`changeset pack --from-publish-plan`, present in 3.0.3's `dist/pack.mjs`), prints name · version · dist-tag · intra-group ranges per package and restores the tree (`git restore --source=HEAD --staged --worktree`, then only the untracked files it created). It reads packed manifests, as the amendment requires. The preflight job runs it on every dispatch (:2267). The output recorded on the card (dev report 6676176273): 109 members, version `0.0.0-next-20261106032733`, planned 109, packed 109, 540 intra-group ranges checked, 0 guard problems, 1 preflight refusal (service-push), 611 paths moved and restored. `pnpm pack` does not run `prepublishOnly` (the three manifests that carry one are untouched by the pack), so the unbuilt preflight tree packs. Acceptance item 1 is met at the amendment's count of 109, not the ruling's 69.

**Docs consumer — met.** `docs/releases-maintenance.md:193-204` adds the snapshot `next` row with the version shape, the approval-screen name, both refusals and the AI-seat prohibition; :238-241 names `snapshot_next` on the Run-workflow paragraph. The claim that the next stable moves `next` back up holds against `release-dist-tags.mjs:238-239` (any pre-release below the reference moves).

**Findings in ①.**
- should-fix (RC cycle, the tree read): both `snapshot-next.mjs preflight` runs read `.changeset/pre.json` from the *selected* commit's tree — the preflight after `git checkout --detach "$commit"` (:2240 then :2261), the publish job on its `ref: C` checkout (:2358). A `pre.json` landed on `main` after C, or during the approval wait, is not seen, and the snapshot would then overwrite the cycle's `next` (the next RC publish would move it back, and `latest` is never touched). The amendment's phrase is "while `.changeset/pre.json` says `mode: pre`", and "the cycle owns the channel" reads on `main`'s state. Fix: also read `origin/main:.changeset/pre.json` — in the preflight before the detach (the dispatched head is the checkout) and in the publish job from the `refs/remotes/origin/main` it already fetched for the ancestry check — and refuse on `mode: pre` there too.
- should-fix (lag vs loss on a snapshot): `release-snapshot-publish.sh` starts no npm record (`release-verify-npm.mjs --start-npm-record` / `npm_config_logs_dir`, which `release-publish.sh` does), so when `release-verify-npm.mjs` (:2419) fails on a snapshot its text can only say "npm's answer was not recorded: the publish did not go through scripts/release-publish.sh". The verdict is unaffected (the record never decides it), so this is diagnostic only.

### ② Semver level

`skip-changeset` is right: the diff touches `.github/workflows/**`, `scripts/**` and `docs/**` only; no package `files[]` ships any of it, so nothing publishes from a released package. The PR body's `Clause-②: no` is well-formed (AGENTS.md: `yes|no` plus at most one arm; no arm is allowed) and true — no published-spec capability widens or narrows; `Metadata-protocol: none` is right. `Part of #30591` is right: the card's acceptance item 2 (the first real snapshot's `npm view` reading) and the Tier H hand-off outlive this merge, and the first snapshot cannot run until `@objectstack/service-push` debuts through the stable lane. `PR-body guards` concluded `success` on the head.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Tier H, governed path `.github/workflows/release.yml`: landing waits for this record and the maintainer's merge (Prime Directive 14); nothing here approves anything.
- Prime Directive 15 holds in the tree: no seat can reach the lane through the fleet-write relay (inputs refused by name), the publish needs a human dispatch and a human `release` approval, and the docs and the job header say so. The maintainer's first real approval is the first snapshot — not before service-push debuts.
- The lane runs the *selected* commit's copies of `snapshot-next.mjs`, `release-snapshot-publish.sh` and the tree's tooling (the stable publish documents the same shape: "a release is built by the version commit's own tooling"). Consequence after this PR merges: dispatches refuse with a missing-module error until a distance-zero green commit carries the PR. Fail-closed; no action.
- Not decided by the amendment and not built here: the runtime image (no `docker-publish.yml` in the lane; pinned out), the form of the daily proposal, the channel's fate after the trial.
- `tagOverrideProblems` does not read `$HOME/.npmrc` (where the job appends the token); the CLI `--tag` beats an npmrc `tag=` anyway, and `publishConfig.tag`, the one override that beats the CLI, is checked. Note only.

### ④ Design judgment

The dev's open points, each against the tree and the amendment:

1. **The commit reading — right.** The amendment names `scheduled-full-run.mjs --release-gate` as the reader; its rule (:805-840) reads `schedule` and `push` runs on `main`, passes over `cancelled`, takes the newest run on the nearest commit, and passes only when every workflow's chosen run is `success`. "The head commit of the newest green full-battery run" under that reader is the newest first-parent commit at which both `CI` and `Lint & Type Check` decide green at distance zero — what `selectSnapshotCommit` returns, including its refusal of a commit where only one workflow ran (self-test :2673-2681).
2. **The combined inputs — right.** Shown under exclusivity above; `force` is never read by the lane and `refresh_version_pr` wins over it, both pinned.
3. **No Docker image — right.** The amendment lists the image under "Not decided here"; the lane builds none and the self-test forbids `docker-publish.yml` in it.
5a. **The publish through `scripts/release-snapshot-publish.sh` — right.** The amendment prescribes the command, not where it lives; the script is the ruling's one line after the stable lane's dist-tooling refusal, with `npm_config_globalconfig` unset for the measured reason in `release-publish.sh`, and the self-test pins the job to one call and the script to one publish line.
5b. **`release-spec-changes.sh --generate` then `--verify` — right.** `--generate` is the pre-release half (registry projections, no per-release section, nothing read from npm) and leaves the `registry-only` marker that `--verify` reads as `--no-release-section`; `RELEASE_VERSION` is set (:2389). `--prepare`/`--attach` are the stable lane's and are pinned out.
5c. **The version shape `0.0.0-next-<timestamp>` — right, and it is what the amendment assumes.** With no `snapshot` block in `.changeset/config.json` (`snapshot: null`), changesets' template-less default is `0.0.0-next-YYYYMMDDHHMMSS`; a fixed group takes one version (109 at one version in the dry run). Line 7 of the amendment relies on "a snapshot version is a pre-release below every stable" so the stable dist-tag step moves `next` back up — `0.0.0-next-*` satisfies that and `release-dist-tags.mjs:238-239` moves it. App repos pinning `next` resolve by dist-tag, and the packed manifests carry exact snapshot versions for every intra-group range (540 checked), so an install of `@objectstack/cli@next` resolves the whole group. `snapshot.useCalculatedVersion` is not configured and would be refused (`versionProblems` refuses `18.4.0-next-…`, self-test :749) — right, because a calculated shape sorts above the current stable and the dist-tag step's rule would then not move `next` back.
5d. **The before/after dist-tag verify — right.** The "before" record is read after the approval and before the publish (:2358), the "after" after it (:2427); only `latest` moving onto the snapshot is an incident, another stable's move is a note, `next` not yet on the snapshot is pending with a bounded retry.

Against the amendment's own closing list ("What stays forbidden"): no path from `push`/`schedule`, no widening by `force`/`refresh_version_pr`, no stable publishing job on a snapshot dispatch, no debut, no cut in pre mode (with the should-fix on which tree is read), no `latest`, no tag, no Release, no Version Packages PR touch, no version bump on `main`. The stable lane is unchanged: the only non-comment edits to stable jobs are the three subtractive `if:` conjuncts.

**Must-fix:** none.
**Should-fix:** (1) read `.changeset/pre.json` at `origin/main`'s head as well as at the selected commit, in both jobs; (2) start the npm answer record in `release-snapshot-publish.sh` so a failed read-back can tell lag from loss.

Implemented-by: `claude/issue-30591-next-snapshot-lane`
Reviewed-by: `session_017ihL2ebbZkr2QAEG1x7UC8`

**VERDICT: PASS**

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `3efd5932e5e82dc1215619d814539643bf25d807`
Local-runs: none
Scope: .github/workflows/release.yml, .github/workflows/lint.yml, docs/releases-maintenance.md, scripts/ci/scheduled-full-run.mjs, scripts/ci/snapshot-next.mjs, scripts/pm/fleet-write/validate.mjs, scripts/release-snapshot-publish.sh + scripts/release-publish.sh, scripts/release-verify-npm.mjs, docs/adr/0125-release-approval-gate-replaces-the-typed-version.md (Amendment 2026-11-05)

Delta record on PR #30799, following the round-1 record (6676411003, PASS on `75a0ac45f8`). Judged: `git diff 75a0ac45f8b60d523b233fcbef0ecf53d6968932..3efd5932e5e82dc1215619d814539643bf25d807` — one commit, `3efd5932e5`, fast-forward (no rebase, no force-push), 4 files: `.github/workflows/release.yml` +12 −6 (step `run:` lines and comments only), `docs/releases-maintenance.md` +1 −1, `scripts/ci/snapshot-next.mjs` +237 −24, `scripts/release-snapshot-publish.sh` +26 −2 — plus what it touches. Round-1 judgments on everything the delta leaves untouched stand. All line numbers are the new head's.

**Check-runs on the head:** at the last poll, 39 `success`, 10 `skipped`, 0 `failure`, 7 still `in_progress` (`Test UI`, `Test Core (1/8)`, `Test Core (2/8)`, `Lint UI`, `Type Check UI`, `Build & E2E UI`, `Lint · PM dispatch-gates`). The one check that exercises the delta's code, `Lint · CI, release & engine gates`, concluded `success` with its steps `Snapshot lane guard self-test` (`snapshot-next.mjs --self-test`, now 13 batteries including the two new ones) `success`, `Release version-commit selection self-test` `success` and `Lane verdict` `success`. Also green: `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `PR-body guards (claim · duplicate · Part-of · single-writer path)`, `Lint · scoped · tooling self-tests`, `Lint · ESLint`. The seven unfinished runs are UI/core test shards and the PM dispatch-gates lane, none of which the delta's four files feed except through `check:pm-dispatch-gates` (which the dev reports exit 0 locally; its CI conclusion is pending).

### ① Derived judgments

**S1 — the RC cycle read at main's tip: closes the gap.**
- Mechanism (`scripts/ci/snapshot-next.mjs`): `MAIN_REF = 'refs/remotes/origin/main'` (:121). `readPreJsonAt(root, ref)` (:371-386) accepts only a plain ref spelling, resolves `${ref}^{commit}` with `git rev-parse --verify --quiet` and **throws** when it does not resolve (:373-374), `ls-tree`s `.changeset/pre.json` at the ref (empty → `null`, i.e. absent; a non-zero exit throws), then `git show`s it. `preCycleRefusals` (:162-170) applies `preModeRefusal` to both texts and refuses on `mode: pre` at either, each refusal naming where it was read. `preflight` (:395-399) reads `{ atCommit: tree's pre.json, atMain: readPreJsonAt(root, mainRef) }` by default; `dryRun` (:568) passes `mainRef` through to `preflight`.
- Fail-closed on an unresolvable ref: the throw propagates out of `preflight()`; the CLI's `preflight` mode catches it as `::error::snapshot preflight NOT MEASURED` and returns `EXIT_PREREQUISITE_NOT_MET` (:1150-1155); the `dry-run` mode's catch does the same (:1197-1201). A `--main-ref` with no value (`argValue` → `''`) fails the spelling check and refuses the same way. Nothing reads "unresolvable" as "absent". The scratch-repo cases of the new battery (:804, git reader at :840-850) pin it: `main` has `pre.json` while the detached older tree has none (:840), a ref whose tree lacks the file reads as absent, "a main ref that does not resolve throws (NOT MEASURED), never reads as absent" (:842), and the default `preflight` on the detached scratch tree refuses on `main`'s cycle (:850).
- Both jobs carry it, pinned: preflight job `preflight --main-ref refs/remotes/origin/main` (`release.yml:2264`) and `dry-run --main-ref refs/remotes/origin/main` (:2270); publish job `preflight --main-ref refs/remotes/origin/main --record …` (:2364). `snapshotWiring` (:738-742) refuses any `preflight`/`dry-run` call in either job without ` --main-ref refs/remotes/origin/main`, with firing cases for each of the three call sites (:985-986).
- **Is the preflight's reading sound — main read after the detach, from the ref the checkout fetched before it?** Yes. The preflight job's `actions/checkout@v7` runs with `fetch-depth: 0` (:2205) on the dispatched ref (`refs/heads/main`, enforced by the step's own `GITHUB_REF` check). A full-history checkout fetches `+refs/heads/*:refs/remotes/origin/*`, so `refs/remotes/origin/main` exists and names the dispatched tip (`GITHUB_SHA`). `git checkout --quiet --detach "$commit"` (:2240) moves `HEAD` and the worktree only; a remote-tracking ref is never moved by a checkout, and nothing between :2240 and :2264 fetches or updates refs (`setup-workspace` is Node/pnpm/install, `check:changeset-fixed` reads the tree). So the read at :2264 sees `main` exactly as it stood at dispatch — the newest state of `main` the job can know, and strictly newer than or equal to the selected commit. The same ref is what the stable lane's own guard (`:1759`, `merge-base --is-ancestor … refs/remotes/origin/main` after a `ref:`-SHA `fetch-depth: 0` checkout) already relies on, and what the snapshot publish job's ancestry guard reads (:2340): in that job the checkout happens after the approval, so :2364 sees a cycle entered during the approval wait. The residual window is the minutes between the publish job's checkout and `changeset publish`; the amendment's "before any deployment is queued" and "after the click" readings are both covered, and changesets' own pre-mode refusal of `--snapshot`/`--tag` remains the backstop for the selected tree.
- Note (not a finding): at the preflight the two readings differ only when a `pre.json` landed on `main` between the selected commit and the dispatched tip; at the publish job they differ whenever one landed during the wait. Both are the exact cases round 1 named.

**S2 — npm's answer record in the snapshot publish: mirrors the stable script, keeps the exit, touches nothing stable.**
- `scripts/release-snapshot-publish.sh` now runs, in order: the dist-tooling scan (:48), then `NPM_RECORD_DIR="$(node scripts/release-verify-npm.mjs --start-npm-record)"`, `export npm_config_logs_dir="$NPM_RECORD_DIR"`, `export npm_config_logs_max=100000` (:59-61), then `publish_status=0; changeset publish --tag next --no-git-tag || publish_status=$?` (:63-64), then `release-verify-npm.mjs --npm-answers || echo "::warning::…"` (:68-69), then `exit "$publish_status"` (:71). That is `release-publish.sh`'s sequence line for line, minus the tag push. Under `set -euo pipefail` a failed `--start-npm-record` aborts before the publish (same as stable). The record lands under `RUNNER_TEMP`, where the job's existing `release-verify-npm.mjs` read-back (:2422) finds it; the record never decides that verdict.
- Pinned: `PUBLISH_LINE` (:100) is now the `|| publish_status=$?` form and `snapshotWiring` requires exactly one publish line equal to it (:708-710) plus the order scan → record → logs vars → publish → `--npm-answers` → `exit "$publish_status"` (:712-725); firing cases remove the record, move it before the scan, drop the answers, drop the exit (:977-984).
